name: Central Discoid Corneal Dystrophy
aliases: Central Discoid Dystrophy of the Cornea

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Slit-Lamp Diagnostic Criteria for Central Discoid Corneal Dystrophy

criteria.description: Presence of a central, discoid-shaped, grayish-white corneal opacity localized in the anterior stroma
Bilateral symmetric corneal involvement without significant inflammation
Characteristic slit-lamp biomicroscopy findings showing well-demarcated discoid lesions with clear surrounding cornea
Positive family history suggestive of autosomal dominant inheritance (supportive but not mandatory)
No signs of corneal inflammation or vascularization

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of central discoid corneal opacity with bilateral involvement and characteristic slit-lamp findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is not routinely available; diagnosis is primarily clinical.

searchTerms: small loss of sharpness in vision
no new blood vessels in cornea

occasional.symptomName: Mild ocular discomfort or foreign body sensation

searchTerms: blurred vision that comes and goes

occasional.symptomName: Mild corneal stromal haze beyond central lesion

imaging: Slit-lamp biomicroscopy revealing central discoid stromal opacities
Anterior segment optical coherence tomography (AS-OCT) showing localized stromal hyperreflectivity
genetic: No specific gene identified; possible autosomal dominant inheritance pattern reported
other: Corneal topography may show localized irregular astigmatism
Absence of corneal vascularization or inflammation

distinguishingFeatures: Central corneal opacity but often associated with prior trauma or inflammation
Lack of bilateral symmetric discoid lesions
Diffuse stromal haze with multiple small opacities
Involvement of entire cornea rather than central discoid lesion
Often associated with corneal thinning and endothelial changes
Discrete granular opacities scattered throughout corneal stroma
Usually multiple lesions rather than single discoid opacity
Genetic testing may identify TGFBI mutations

redFlags: Onset of pain or severe photophobia indicating possible secondary infection
references: Krachmer JH, Mannis MJ, Holland EJ. Cornea: Fundamentals, Diagnosis and Management. 4th ed. Elsevier; 2011.
Weiss JS, Møller HU, Lisch W, et al. IC3D classification of corneal dystrophies—edition 2. Cornea. 2015;34(2):117-159.
